record.paper_title: Singularity Theorems in General Relativity: Achievements and Open Questions.
record.original_question: Do the singularity theorems still leave room for constructing cosmologically realistic universes that are geodesically complete and free of singularities, even while satisfying the usual causality and energy conditions that appear in classical general relativity?

evidence.quote: Of course, the model is not realistic in the sense that it cannot describe the actual Universe —for instance, the isotropy of the cosmic background radiation cannot be explained—, but the question arises of whether or not there is room left over by the singularity theorems to construct geodesically complete realistic universes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider classical general relativity in four spacetime dimensions, where a spacetime is a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian manifold (M, g) satisfying the Einstein field equations for some matter content. Recall that:

- (M, g) is said to be singularity-free in the geodesic sense if it is geodesically complete, i.e. every (timelike, null, and spacelike) inextendible geodesic can be extended to all values of its affine parameter.
- The standard causality conditions are those used in the classical singularity theorems (for instance, the chronology condition, the strong causality condition, or the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface / global hyperbolicity).
- The standard energy conditions are the pointwise conditions on the stress-energy tensor T_{ab} (or equivalently, via Einstein's equations, on the Ricci tensor) used in the classical singularity theorems: the weak energy condition T_{ab} u^a u^b ≥ 0 for all timelike u^a, the dominant energy condition, the strong energy condition (T_{ab} − ½ T g_{ab}) u^a u^b ≥ 0, and the null energy condition T_{ab} k^a k^b ≥ 0 for all null k^a.
- A cosmological spacetime is taken to be "realistic" if it can plausibly describe our observed Universe; in particular, it should accommodate the observed large-scale near-isotropy and homogeneity (including a mechanism compatible with the isotropy of the cosmic microwave background) and the basic features of cosmic expansion.

Problem. Determine whether there exist exact solutions (M, g, T_{ab}) of the Einstein field equations with a physically reasonable matter content satisfying simultaneously all of the following:

(i) (M, g) is geodesically complete (no singularities of geodesic-incompleteness type);
(ii) (M, g) satisfies the standard causality conditions invoked in the classical singularity theorems;
(iii) the matter content satisfies the standard energy conditions (in particular the strong and dominant energy conditions);
(iv) (M, g) is cosmologically realistic in the sense above, i.e. it is compatible with the observed isotropy and homogeneity on large scales and provides an account of the isotropy of the cosmic microwave background.

Equivalently: do the classical singularity theorems leave room for cosmologically realistic, geodesically complete, singularity-free universes that nonetheless satisfy the usual causality and energy hypotheses of those theorems?
artifact.status_search_result: Singularity-free, geodesically complete cosmological solutions of Einstein's equations satisfying the standard causality and energy conditions are known to exist (e.g., Senovilla's 1990 cylindrical radiation-filled model and later inhomogeneous generalizations). However, no such known model is fully realistic: in particular, none reproduce the observed large-scale isotropy and homogeneity, including the isotropy of the cosmic microwave background, while keeping all classical energy and causality conditions. Recent work (bouncing, emergent, and eternally inflating FRW scenarios) either requires violations of the null/strong energy conditions or remains only partly realistic. The existence of a fully realistic geodesically complete cosmological model within classical GR therefore appears to remain an open question.

status_evidence.title: Geodesically complete universes
status_evidence.snippet: All non-trivial geodesically complete FRW spacetimes necessarily require an epoch of accelerated expansion; the price of eternal inflation in GR is a period of NEC violation.
status_evidence.claim: Realistic FRW geodesic completeness in classical GR generically conflicts with the null energy condition, indicating the question is not resolved affirmatively under the standard energy conditions.

status_evidence.title: Inflationary resolution of the initial singularity
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of nonsingular FRW cosmologies into bouncing, emergent, and asymptotically emergent types, all requiring some form of energy condition modification.
status_evidence.claim: Known singularity-free realistic FRW scenarios require violation or weakening of standard energy conditions.

status_evidence.title: On Singularity Free Cosmological Models (Senovilla 1990 and follow-ups)
status_evidence.snippet: Senovilla's cylindrical radiation model is geodesically complete and satisfies energy and causality conditions but is inhomogeneous and not realistic (cannot explain CMB isotropy).
status_evidence.claim: Existence of non-realistic singularity-free models is established; the realistic case remains open.
